messages:
taylor: Quick proposal for span naming + attrs for LLM inference traces — trying to keep span names low-cardinality and attributes rich enough for dashboards/rollouts. Thoughts?

priya: +1 to low-cardinality names. what's the suggested pattern?

 taylor: idea 1: always use a canonical name `inference.request` and then attach semantic attrs for model/operation. e.g.
```
span.name = \"inference.request\"
attributes:
  redwood.model.name = \"gpt4o-mini\"
  redwood.model.variant = \"q8_0\"
  redwood.inference.op = \"generate\"
  redwood.tokens.prompt = 120
  redwood.tokens.completion = 45
  redwood.kv.cache_hits = 1
  redwood.routing.policy = \"price-pref\"
```
This keeps grouping in traces simple while letting dashboards filter by attrs.

sam: I'm worried about high-cardinality attrs like full model ARN or rollout IDs. we should sanitize model identifiers (just short name + version) and avoid user identifiers.

jordan: Agreed. Also, for rollout experiments we need an attribute but keep it bounded: `redwood.rollout_tag = \"canary-v3\"` (string but limited set). Do not put rollout UUIDs on every span.

 lia: For dashboards we really want model in the span name sometimes so engineers can eyeball spans quickly in the UI. Can we compromise? e.g. `inference.request/<model>` but only allow short token (no build ids).

 taylor: That is a tradeoff. If we do `inference.request/gpt4o-mini` we increase cardinality by model count (which is manageable). But don't include variant or quantization in the name — keep those as attrs. Proposed canonical forms: either:
- `inference.request` (lowest cardinality) OR
- `inference.request/<model>` (low-medium cardinality)
We'll pick one globally.

 priya: Ops: retention/export rules need clarity. We shouldn't export raw token counts to long-term hot storage for privacy and cost. Proposal: keep full attributes for 7 days in the OTLP ingest, then roll up to metrics/aggregates (tokens per model per hour) for 90+ days.

 sam: +1. Also redact prompt text and any PII before attaching attributes. Add a mandatory lint step in the SDK that errors when `redwood.prompt.text` is present.

 taylor: Agreed on lint. Also propose a small keyset (will be enforced by schema):
```
redwood.model.name (string, short)
redwood.model.version (string)
redwood.inference.op (enum: generate, embed, rerank, embed_stream)
redwood.tokens.prompt (int, optional)
redwood.tokens.completion (int, optional)
redwood.kv.cache_hits (int)
redwood.kv.cache_misses (int)
redwood.routing.policy (string)
redwood.rollout_tag (string, optional)
redwood.error (bool)
```
Keep keys prefixed with `redwood.*` to avoid collisions.

 jordan: about exporters: maybe have two exporters — `redwood-hot` (7d retention, full attr set) and `redwood-aggregate` (long-term metrics only). We can route spans with `redwood.tokens.*` to hot then drop for archive.

 lia: How do we store sampling decisions? need an attr `redwood.trace_sample_decision = \"keep\"|\"drop\"` so downstream pipelines can reconstruct.

 taylor: yes add sampling attr. Also, for KV cache hits the attribute semantics: `redwood.kv.cache_hits` is number of times we read from prefix cache during this request, `redwood.kv.prefetch` boolean if a prefetch occurred.

 priya: Example of a synthetic span (python):
```
with tracer.start_span("inference.request") as s:
  s.set_attribute('redwood.model.name', 'gpt4o-mini')
  s.set_attribute('redwood.model.version', '2026-03-01')
  s.set_attribute('redwood.inference.op', 'generate')
  s.set_attribute('redwood.tokens.prompt', 80)
  s.set_attribute('redwood.tokens.completion', 20)
  s.set_attribute('redwood.kv.cache_hits', 0)
  s.set_attribute('redwood.rollout_tag', 'canary-v3')
```
Don't put the prompt text.

 sam: minor nit: use `int64` for token counts in export schema. Also, add `redwood.model.size = \"13B\"`? that might be useful for cost dashboards.

 taylor: OK add `redwood.model.size` but encourage a small enum: tiny/small/medium/large/xl to keep cardinality low.

 deploy-bot: deploy `telemetry-span-rfc` updated schema -> staging at 2026-03-14T15:20Z :rocket:

 lia: Next steps: 1) pick span-name canonicalization (we should vote: `inference.request` vs `inference.request/<model>`). 2) land schema + SDK lint. 3) exporter routing rules for retention. I'll open an RFC PR with the above suggestions.

 taylor: Thanks. I'll +1 the RFC and add a short example for console dashboards (tokens heatmap by `redwood.model.name` + `redwood.rollout_tag`).

 priya: LGTM — please include the privacy checklist in the RFC.

 sam: fine by me. If we hit cardinality pain we can flip to the pure-canonical name later.

 lia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/842 — feel free to comment. :thumbsup:
